java.assessment: %g expands to U+0022, U+201C, U+201D and U+E121 everywhere it appears, not only in DISPLAY. %s expands to Java regex whitespace plus NBSP, and matching is case-insensitive.
The tag body is [^%s{}%g<>$]+, so every Pattern2 %g member is forbidden inside a tag.
The inline and multiline forms compose the shared tag, stereotype and color grammars. Multiline validity is partial until an endnote/end note terminator is found.
The Description inventory registers named-note, note-on-link and note-on-entity factories. The latter two require on/of/link or a position token and do not share note + whitespace + %g openers.
Attached-note commands require right/left/top/bottom immediately after note whitespace, excluding %g opener overlap.
Link-note commands require optional position followed by on/of link and do not overlap the named-note %g opener.
No matching complete command yields a syntax-error PSystem; an unterminated multiline candidate never becomes an executable step.

rust.assessment: The repaired ownership predicate claims every note + Rust whitespace + %g opener. The successful decoration regex at line 132 excludes only ASCII double quote from tag bodies, so U+201C, U+201D and U+E121 pass parse_named_note_inline before the terminal predicate is consulted.

Inline parse success is committed before terminal ownership validation. Multiline state consumes every later line while in_note is true, but EOF performs no in_note validation and returns an accepted diagram without the note or swallowed declarations/relations.
Inline parse success likewise precedes terminal ownership validation. note_accum consumes all later lines until a terminator, but EOF returns Ok without checking that note_accum remains populated.

causal_assessment.command_selection: No competing Description command factory was found for note + whitespace + a %g opener. The e6edba58 prefix predicate correctly claims malformed openers across U+0022, U+201C, U+201D and U+E121.
causal_assessment.first_disproof: The account treats the four-member %g model as a DISPLAY boundary but Java also substitutes %g inside Stereotag.pattern. Rust's successful decoration regex excludes only U+0022. A tag containing U+201C, U+201D or U+E121 therefore makes Java return syntax error while Rust creates a named note carrying that character in its tag. Because parsing succeeds, looks_like_named_note_inline_command never gets a chance to reject it.
causal_assessment.second_disproof: Java's multiline command remains partial until endnote/end note is found and rejects at EOF. Rust Component in_note and Deployment note_accum consume later declarations and relations as body, then EOF silently discards the unfinished note state and returns Ok.
causal_assessment.conclusion: The implementation repairs the previously reported embedded-DISPLAY escape but does not establish the account's broader invariant that failure anywhere after a uniquely owned opener rejects the candidate.

findings.title: Pattern2 quote characters in tags bypass terminal rejection through the successful parse path
findings.java_provenance: Stereotag.SINGLE is (\$[^%s{}%g<>$]+). Pattern2 transforms %g to U+0022/U+201C/U+201D/U+E121 before CommandFactoryNote matches, so all four are forbidden in a valid tag.
findings.rust_data_flow: named_note_decorations uses [^\s{}\"<>$]+ and therefore forbids only U+0022. parse_named_note_inline returns Some for U+201C/U+201D/U+E121 tag bodies; Component and Deployment commit the note before looks_like_named_note_inline_command is reached.
findings.impact: Six note + whitespace + %g opener commands rejected by Java are accepted as fully formed notes by Rust, directly falsifying terminal rejection after the unique opener.

findings.title: Unterminated multiline named notes are silently accepted at EOF
findings.java_provenance: CommandMultilines2 remains OK_PARTIAL until CommandFactoryNote.END matches. PSystemCommandFactory.isMultilineCommandOk returns no candidate when EOF arrives first, yielding syntax-error output.
findings.rust_data_flow: Component's in_note and Deployment's note_accum consume all following lines, but neither parser checks unfinished note state after its input loop. Both return Ok and silently omit the note plus the later declaration and relation consumed as body.
findings.impact: Malformed multiline openers escape rejection in both reviewed families and can suppress arbitrary later declarations and relations while producing a successful diagram.

findings.title: The second follow-up fixes the previously reported inline opener escape
findings.detail: All eight embedded-%g cases, all eight missing-closer cases and eighteen ordinary malformed suffix cases now reject before later endpoint synthesis in both families.

findings.title: No valid command was rejected
findings.detail: All 32 independent %g opener/closer combinations, eight valid multiline variants and two Java-valid combined stereotype payload probes were accepted by both binaries.

anti_overfit_audit.evidence: The reviewed diff adds a general four-member prefix predicate and two unit cases. declared_residue_assessment: Deployment note-on-link remains outside this review and was not used to reach the verdict.
Java error-page artwork and diagnostic wording were not compared; Java process acceptance/rejection and Rust process/YAML behavior were the oracle.
The quote-bearing tag failures are not a separate command factory: they occur inside CommandFactoryNote's own Stereotag suffix grammar after the exact opener governed by this account.
The EOF failures are an independent multiline ownership defect in the same named-note command state and were required by the requested inline/multiline adversarial matrix.
verdict_reason: REJECT. Revision e6edba58 correctly claims malformed inline openers at note + whitespace + each Pattern2 %g delimiter and rejects the prior embedded-DISPLAY counterexamples. It still accepts six Java-invalid inline commands because Rust's successful tag grammar omits U+201C, U+201D and U+E121 from the forbidden %g set, so terminal rejection is bypassed. It also accepts unterminated multiline named notes in both Component and Deployment, swallowing later declarations and relations before returning success. Any malformed opener accepted by Rust requires rejection under the requested gate.
